attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, in his authorial voice.

semantics.note: Faithful paraphrase. 'Script-based workarounds' stands in for 'MacGuffins'. Labelling it causal fits the chain from hallucinations to tokens to costs, though the sentence is very rhetorical.

contract.note: The readings are reasonable but chosen by the evaluator: the three-month window, mutiny defined as resistance, and modeled gross margins as the unprofitability measure. The speaker gave no cohort or measure, so how these terms are read shapes any result, despite the contract's flag saying otherwise.

evidence.note: Formal impossibility result for general problem solvers. It bears on 'mathematically guaranteed' but says nothing about tokens, bills, mutiny, or margins.
Ties hallucinations to training and evaluation incentives. This narrows the strict-inevitability reading but does not test the economic chain.
GitHub's own disclosure of a switch to usage billing. Different company, and it shows no backlash, hallucination link, or OpenAI/Anthropic margins.
Secondary report of Meta curbing token spend. The cause given is internal tokenmaxxing, not hallucinations. It shows no provider margins, and the controls start in 2027.

reviews.rationale: No evidence connects hallucinations to extra billed tokens, higher customer bills, resistance within a quarter of a pricing change, and negative OpenAI/Anthropic margins. Each item covers at most one fragment, or a different company. Nothing disproves a necessary link either, so the packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. 'Really helpful with research' is a view he attributes to others, but the hallucination claim is his.

semantics.note: Here 'will absolutely' states a universal generalisation, not a dated forecast. The universal scope is kept.

contract.note: The universal reading is the ordinary one; the context says the error is 'certain'. Whether short factual answers count as research, and the evaluator-chosen Q1 2026 window, affect what could decide the claim.

evidence.note: Shows hallucinations across six research agents on deliberately hard tasks. Aggregate scores do not show that every response hallucinates.
All models answered one clinical question correctly under neutral prompts. These are short answers, not full research reports checked in full, and the generation dates are unknown.
Legal-research tools gave some accurate, grounded answers, but the evaluation dates to 2024, outside the window. The listed availability date conflicts with the v1 URL.

reviews.rationale: Proving the universal requires showing that every research output hallucinates, and no item does that. Disproving it requires one fully checked, hallucination-free substantive response from Q1 2026. e2 does not meet the full-response or date test, and e3 falls outside the period. The evidence does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A composite: one present-tense observation ('not happening') plus firm 'will not' forecasts with no deadline. The venture-funding clause is correctly limited to 'real businesses'.

contract.note: The readings of 'cheaper' and 'real businesses', and the two-quarter persistence test, are evaluator choices, but ordinary ones. Whether 'cheaper' means prices or provider costs decides the observation part.

evidence.note: Independent estimate that the price of a given performance level falls about 47% per quarter. It measures customer price, not provider full cost, and does not isolate Q1 2026. It is material counterevidence to a broad reading only.
Anthropic's own disclosure of cheaper serving in September 2026. It falls after the observation window and does not show profitability or a causal effect of data centers.

reviews.rationale: The forecasts have no deadline, and no evidence shows sustained full-cost profitability or cost-covering customer payments caused by added data centers or funding, so no early resolution applies. Under the contextual reading of provider cost, the cost-observation part is not settled. The price evidence uses a different metric and is not specific to the quarter.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assessment in his own post.

semantics.note: The hedge 'not much more than', the benchmark limit, and the claimed purpose are all kept. The intent clause is closer to rhetoric than a testable observation.

contract.note: Reading the second clause as 'little practical advance beyond benchmarks' is the ordinary sense of a sentence that minimises the model to benchmark gains plus hype. The definition of recursive self-improvement is the evaluator's, but standard.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure that it has not reached recursive self-improvement. It is not an independent finding, but it is an admission against the company's interest, and it is dated within the window.
Mozilla, a separate organisation, shipped fixes for 271 Firefox vulnerabilities found with Mythos Preview in April 2026. That is a practical result well beyond benchmark scores.

reviews.rationale: The recursive self-improvement part holds: Anthropic itself disclaims it. The 'not much more than benchmarks' part is contradicted by Mozilla's verified, shipped vulnerability fixes found with Mythos. The marketing-intent part is not established by any item, so it stays untested.
